question: Why does a touch screen work when you touch it?
answer: Under the glass, a layer of indium tin oxide carries an electric current. Your skin conducts electricity, so your finger gives that current a path to the ground and changes the electric field at that spot. The phone reads the change as a touch right there.
move: A touch screen senses a conductor, so it's about conductivity.

web.label: Two side-by-side panels show a sensor field under glass. One panel has a finger held on the screen, and the field changes at that spot. The other has a plastic stick held on the screen, and the field stays steady. Hold buttons let the reader press a finger or a plastic stick to try both.

source: Geopop, “Sai come funziona uno schermo touch screen? FIGO! NON LO SAPEVO” (YouTube, 2021)
